belief: I can't take one more day of this.
origins: When pain, exhaustion, and discouragement pile up, one more day can seem unbearable. This is a human response to overload, and it can also be a warning sign that more support is needed.
teaches: Elijah was so exhausted that he asked God to take his life. God did not scold him. He sent rest, food, and an angel who said, “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you” (1 Kings 19:7). Jesus said, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” “Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you.” Paul adds, “My grace is sufficient for you.” God gives strength for each day, not all at once. If you are thinking of ending your life, call or text 988 now.
self_statements: I do not know how I will get through today.
I just want it to stop.
errors: Believing I can either bear everything or nothing.
Predicting that tomorrow will be unbearable.
Feeling overwhelmed and concluding that I cannot continue.
questions: What exactly feels unbearable right now?
What have I gotten through before that felt impossible?
What is the smallest next step for this hour?
Who can I call or be with right now?
What basic needs, such as food, rest, and medication, need attention?
What does God say to the weary?
truth: I do not have to carry tomorrow today. God gives grace for this day, and I can take the next small step and reach out for help. If I think of harming myself, I will call or text 988 right away.
hw_truths: Jesus gives rest to the weary.
His mercies are new each morning.
I can take the next step.
I can reach out for help.
log: Each day, note one small step you took and one person you contacted.
actions: Reach out to a friend or your doctor.
Eat, hydrate, rest, and take medication as prescribed.
If life feels unbearable, call or text 988 (U.S.).
prayer: Lord, I am so tired. Sustain me today. Send the help I need and let Your grace be enough for this hour. Amen.
